title: "$5" + 1 is 6: a currency symbol is accepted in text converted to a number

source.quote: the string is automatically converted into a corresponding number, as long as the string is a valid representation of a number
source.supports: text in an arithmetic expression converts when it is a valid number; the page does not say which forms are valid

source.quote: The value passed as the text parameter can be in any of the constant, number, date, or time formats recognized by the application or services you are using
source.supports: VALUE accepts the number formats the engine recognizes; the page does not list them

derivation: + converts text to a number when the text is a valid representation of a number. The model culture is en-US, whose currency format is $5, so the text is taken as one of the recognized number formats: 5 + 1 = 6.
alternative: No source says whether a currency symbol is accepted. If it is not, the conversion fails and the query returns an error. This is the least supported of the separator cases.
notes: The column's type is not asserted. If the symbol is accepted the result might also be a fixed decimal.
